recommended.name: Engine-declared route on one address: the Editor asks the engine for its declared locality on the asset plane, then gx_asset_plane::publish_as_package writes one package, hands it over through publish_package and removes it
recommended.summary:
This builds on the judges' winner (design 3), with grafts from designs 2 and 1.

What the operator configures: one value per engine, the existing 'Asset plane' address (Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:66-71; Editor/web/index.html:340-345). The Editor never configures or guesses a locality.

Where the locality comes from: the engine answers a new closed asset-plane read, {"locality":{}}, from the same `locality` field it puts into EngineCapability.locality. The worker serves both planes from one engine object (services/render-engine/worker/src/main.rs:140-145; engine.rs:74, 880-885), and so does the mock (mocks/mock-engine/src/lib.rs:45, 334-356; mocks/mock-engine/src/main.rs:101).

Where the code lives:
- Publish logic moves out of the Tauri crate into gx-editor (new services/editor/src/publish.rs). gx-editor already depends on gx-asset-plane (services/editor/Cargo.toml) and conformance already depends on gx-editor (conformance/Cargo.toml), so cmd_publish and the 5.10 conformance test call the same production function and Tauri never enters the harness.
- Every filesystem step and the locality read sit in Shared/asset-plane, in a new publish_as_package(engine, directory, scene, sources). It (1) reads the declared locality, (2) writes one verified package named by content hash, pid and sequence, (3) calls the existing publish_package(engine, declared, path), so handoff_for stays the only branch (Shared/asset-plane/src/handoff.rs:44-49, 213-256), and (4) removes the package.
- As a result, Editor-side Rust never names a Locality, so R9 cannot regress. It never touches fs, so R2 holds in letter and in spirit. It links no control-plane crate, so R6 holds (tools/check-boundaries.mjs:67-68, 370-373).

The package folder: one folder serves both routes. It is GX_EDITOR_PACKAGE_DIR if set, else a new platform::package_exchange_root() (cache_root()/packages, Shared/contracts/src/platform.rs:95-102). tools/launch-shells.mjs and gx-engine-host give a co-located engine that same folder as --package-dir. The worker still defaults to none, so 5.8 is unchanged. This keeps the 5.8 user decision that the publisher is configured with the engine's directory and nothing about the directory goes on the wire (docs/evidence/5.8/README.md:20-22).

Engine-side enforcement (graft from design 2): one rule in the shared asset-plane server's Package arm (Shared/asset-plane/src/publish.rs:386-394). A peer whose handoff_for(locality()) is ChunkedUpload has no effective package directory, so a stale or forged CoLocated offer to a LAN engine is refused PackageDirectoryNotConfigured by name, for the worker and the mock alike (invariant 45). In addition, gx-render-worker refuses --lan together with --package-dir at startup (usage, exit 2).

What the result carries: the issued content hash is cross-checked against the packaged clone's hash, and PublishResult reports the route and the bytes moved.

The take stays outside the Editor. The 5.10 test lives in conformance, which may hold a control client. It also holds the asset-plane answer equal to EngineCapability.locality on both real workers and on both mocks (invariants 27, 45, 47).

This needs user decisions on two points: (a) a one-field asset-plane locality read, and (b) rewording 5.10's 'from the capability exchange'. The control plane is closed to the Editor twice: by R6, and since 5.7 because the control port authorises only Role::Playout (Shared/control-plane/src/message.rs:93-95).

Process note: jg returned no output, so discovery was by direct reads. During this pass the C: temp volume reported 0 MB free and one grep failed with 'No space left on device'. The implementer must free space before building or running the gate.
recommended.package_build:
(1) The document. cmd_publish keeps its signature (endpoint: String, target: SceneTarget; Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:587-602). It clones the target document under the workspace lock, as today, through Workspace::document (services/editor/src/command.rs:350).

(2) The package sources. Under the asset-store lock, cmd_publish calls gx_editor::publish::package_sources(&scene, &AssetStore) -> Result<Vec<PackageSource>, Refusal>. It handles each scene.assets item:
- checksum None: PackageAssetNotPackaged{asset_id, path} (Shared/contracts/src/lib.rs:545). That is the refusal write_package itself gives (Shared/asset-plane/src/package.rs:274-283). It is returned before any file or socket exists.
- store.cache_path(hash) is unreadable: AssetMissing{hash}.
- re-hashing the file gives a different hash: AssetHashMismatch. This keeps 5.9's re-hash-before-send rule from scene_asset_bytes (Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:272-297).
- otherwise: PackageSource{path: item.path, source: store.cache_path(hash)}, de-duplicated by library path, because write_package refuses duplicate paths (package.rs:253-271).
Sources are verified import-cache files only; the project folder is never read (5.9's rule).

(3) The revision pin. With no lock held, gx_editor::publish::publish_document(endpoint, scene, &sources, &package_directory) does the following:
- It parses the endpoint, refusing InvalidEndpoint before any socket opens.
- It pins the owned clone only: scene.revision.get_or_insert(Revision(1)). write_package needs a pin (package.rs:142-146). The engine issues its own revision (services/render-engine/worker/src/engine.rs:398-404), and the content hash leaves out the top-level revision (Shared/contracts/src/scene.rs:1535-1553). This is not an EditorCommand and not an R3 mutator, and the workspace document is untouched.
- It records expected = clone.content_hash().
- It calls gx_asset_plane::publish_as_package(addr, &package_directory, &clone, &sources).

(4) publish_as_package. This is new in Shared/asset-plane/src/handoff.rs, next to publish_package:
- (a) It calls declared_locality(engine) first, so an unreachable or pre-5.10 engine leaves no file behind.
- (b) It runs create_dir_all(directory).
- (c) It names the file <content_hash hex>-<pid>-<seq>.gpxpkg, with seq from a static AtomicU64. That is at most about 103 characters, under MAX_COMPONENT_LEN 128 (Shared/contracts/src/platform.rs:35). The name never comes from user text or the scene id, which may contain '/' (ADR-0002 B.3; services/editor/src/project.rs:357-366). It is unique per publish, so no package is replaced in place (invariants 7 and 30).
- (d) It calls write_package(&path, scene, sources, None), which builds the candidate, read_package-verifies it and then renames (package.rs:119-205; gx_fs::write_atomic_verified).
- (e) It calls publish_package(engine, declared, &path). LocalPath sends the absolute path and moves 0 asset bytes; the engine re-checks containment after canonicalisation and re-hashes everything (handoff.rs:101-142). ChunkedUpload reads the package back, re-hashes it, and sends only the missing bytes and then the scene (handoff.rs:240-254).
- (f) It calls remove_file(&path) after Published, after a refusal and after a transfer error alike. This is best effort: a failed removal is reported in the result, not turned into an error. The engine read the package inside the request and keeps no path (handoff.rs:10-15; publish.rs:386-394), so nothing re-reads the file.
- (g) It returns DocumentPublication{package: PathBuf, packaged_hash: ContentHash, publication: PackagePublication}. This new wrapper leaves 5.8's exhaustive PackagePublication patterns (conformance/src/package_handoff.rs:155-156) untouched. Failures come back as a new DocumentPublishError{Locality(PublishClientError), LocalityRefused(PublishRefusal), Write(PackageError), Publish(PackagePublishError)}, so PackagePublishError itself is unchanged.

(5) Mapping the result. gx_editor::publish maps the result to Published{take_id, revision, content_hash, handoff, transferred_bytes}.
- If the issued content_hash differs from expected, it returns a named Protocol error that names both hashes and says not to take that revision. This guards the shared-directory window recorded as the 5.8 known gap.
- Errors stay distinct (invariants 17 and 59):
  - Connect: Unreachable.
  - Transfer Refused, any Refused reply (PackageRefused included) and LocalityRefused: PublishRefused. For PackageDirectoryNotConfigured and PackagePathOutsideDirectory the shell appends the Editor's package folder to the detail.
  - Write: the new EditorError::WritePackage{path, detail}, or the Refusal for PackageError::Refused.
  - Anything else: Protocol.

(6) Where the package folder comes from. It is resolved once in the shell's run() and held in ShellState as Result<PathBuf, Refusal>:
- GX_EDITOR_PACKAGE_DIR made absolute, if set; this follows the GX_* convention (Shared/asset-plane/src/fonts/link.rs:934);
- otherwise gx_contracts::platform::package_exchange_root(). An unavailable root is the existing PlatformDirectoryUnavailable, which refuses before any socket opens.
On a co-located machine, tools/launch-shells.mjs creates target/dev-packages, passes --package-dir to the worker (it passes only --port today, line 101) and passes GX_EDITOR_PACKAGE_DIR to the Editor child. The engine host passes --package-dir package_exchange_root() in spawn_args (services/render-engine/host/src/main.rs:32, empty today; only --port and --recovery-journal are reserved, host/src/lib.rs:133-142). On a LAN machine the same folder is simply the Editor's outbox.

(7) What is retired. Editor/shell's publish, publish_with_assets and scene_asset_bytes (lib.rs:267-373) are removed. A pub fn publish_with_sources(endpoint, directory, scene, &sources) -> Result<PublishResult, EditorError> maps errors and is what both cmd_publish and the shell tests call, so there is one command path (invariant 60).
wire_and_contract_changes: Asset plane: a new closed request {"locality":{}}, deny_unknown_fields, added to parse_request's exactly-one set (Shared/asset-plane/src/publish.rs:453-514). A new AssetRequest::Locality arm answers from the peer under a brief lock, as fetch does. A new reply type LocalityReply (tag `reply`, camelCase) has two arms: Declared{locality: Locality} and Refused(PublishRefusal). It is Rust-only like PublishReply, with no ts-rs export, no codegen and no R7 exposure.

AssetPublishPeer gains the REQUIRED method fn locality(&self) -> Locality, with no default. It is implemented by the worker Engine (engine.rs:854), MockEngine (lib.rs:334), conformance RecordingPeer (editor_commands.rs:103, delegating) and the two asset-plane test peers (handoff.rs:332, publish.rs:527).

Shared asset-plane server rule, a behaviour change with no wire change. In handle_publish's Package arm (publish.rs:386-394), the effective directory is None when handoff_for(peer.locality()) is ChunkedUpload. A by-path offer to a LAN-declared engine is then refused PackageRefused{PackageDirectoryNotConfigured}, the existing refusal, even if the peer holds a directory. One rule covers the worker and the mock alike (invariant 45). 5.8's forced-path check against the LAN worker still gets the same refusal (conformance/src/package_handoff.rs:261-274).

gx-render-worker CLI: --lan together with --package-dir is a usage error, exit 2 (services/render-engine/worker/src/main.rs:50-54, 72-103, usage). No existing caller combines them (conformance/src/main.rs:457-462).

New public client gx_asset_plane::declared_locality(engine) -> Result<LocalityReply, PublishClientError>. Also new: gx_asset_plane::publish_as_package(engine, directory: &Path, scene: &SceneDocument, sources: &[PackageSource]) -> Result<DocumentPublication, DocumentPublishError>, plus DocumentPublication{package, packaged_hash, publication: PackagePublication} and DocumentPublishError{Locality, LocalityRefused, Write, Publish}. All are re-exported from Shared/asset-plane/src/lib.rs. AssetHandoff gains Serialize, camelCase: localPath | chunkedUpload. publish_package, handoff_for, open_package_in, PackagePublication, PackagePublishError and the {package:{path}} request are unchanged.

gx-contracts: a new pub fn platform::package_exchange_root() -> Result<PathBuf, Refusal>, equal to cache_root()/packages. No new type and no new Refusal variant. The design reuses PackageAssetNotPackaged, AssetMissing, AssetHashMismatch, PackageDirectoryNotConfigured, PackagePathOutsideDirectory and PlatformDirectoryUnavailable.

Unchanged: the control plane, EngineCapability, ClientRequest, Scope/Role (5.7), generated TS and schemas, and every port bind (R8). Nothing about the package directory goes on the wire (5.8 user decision).

New gx-editor module services/editor/src/publish.rs (pub mod publish) with package_sources(&SceneDocument, &AssetStore) -> Result<Vec<PackageSource>, Refusal>, publish_document(endpoint: &str, scene: SceneDocument, sources: &[PackageSource], directory: &Path) -> Result<Published, PublishFailure>, Published{take_id, revision, content_hash, handoff: AssetHandoff, transferred_bytes} and PublishFailure{InvalidEndpoint, Unreachable, NotSent(Refusal), EngineRefused(PublishRefusal), WritePackage{path, detail}, Protocol}. No Locality appears anywhere in its source.

Editor shell: cmd_publish keeps its parameters, so R1 and R4 are unchanged. PublishResult gains handoff ('localPath'|'chunkedUpload') and transferredBytes. EditorError gains writePackage{path, detail}. ShellState gains package_directory. There is no new Tauri command, so SHELL_READ and generate_handler! are unchanged. publish, publish_with_assets and scene_asset_bytes are removed, and publish_with_sources is added.

Editor web: the hand-mirrored PublishResult interface (Editor/web/main.ts:218-225) gains handoff and transferredBytes. Both publish call sites (main.ts:4640-4670, 4834-4870) log the route and bytes verbatim, and describe() gains writePackage. The web never receives a Locality, so R9's TS rule (check-boundaries.mjs:375-378) cannot trip.

Deployment configuration, not wire. The GX_EDITOR_PACKAGE_DIR environment variable reaches the Editor child. tools/launch-shells.mjs passes --package-dir target/dev-packages to the worker; its start() gains an env option. services/render-engine/host/src/main.rs passes --package-dir package_exchange_root() to workers it spawns; adopted engines keep their flags.

rule_risks: USER DECISION, new wire. The 5.8 decision 'Nothing new goes on the wire or into EngineCapability' sits under 'A co-located publisher is configured with the engine's package directory' (docs/evidence/5.8/README.md:20-22), so it is scoped to the directory. memory.md paraphrases it more broadly, however. The user must confirm that a one-field asset-plane locality read is allowed.

USER DECISION, wording. 5.10 says the Editor 'reads the engine's declared locality from the capability exchange' (GrapiX-Build-Plan.md:317). Under R6 (check-boundaries.mjs:370-373) and 5.7 (message.rs:93-95) that cannot be executed by any Editor-side code. The row, progress.html and the doc comments at capability.rs:1-6 and handoff.rs:6-8 must change.

One declaration, two carriers (invariants 27, 45, 47). Three things mitigate the risk: both carriers read one field per peer; AssetPublishPeer::locality has no default; and conformance checks agreement on two real workers and both mocks. Adding a default later would defeat the check, so the doc comment on the method must say so.

Invariant 55 and authentication. The asset plane is unauthenticated and binds loopback even with --lan (worker main.rs:134-139), so locality becomes readable by any local process. Tier, clock and reference stay control-only. Phase 14 must authenticate the asset plane, this read included, before it is exposed beyond loopback.

Behaviour change from 5.9. A co-located engine started by hand without --package-dir now refuses every Editor publish by name (PackageDirectoryNotConfigured); 5.9's chunked publish succeeded. The launcher and the host pass the folder, but the running dev pair must be restarted once through the updated launcher. This deliberately has no fallback to chunked: falling back would be probing (capability.rs:4-6) and a silent substitution (invariant 18).

Behaviour change from 5.9. An asset with no content hash yet, which scene_asset_bytes skipped (Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:278), is now refused PackageAssetNotPackaged before any connection. This is consistent with invariant 29 but visible to authors.

Engine behaviour change on the 5.8 surface. A LAN-declared peer ignores any package directory, and the worker refuses `--lan --package-dir`. Today the Package arm checks only the directory (publish.rs:386-394). The user should approve this hardening.

Residual staleness between the locality read and the publish, which are two connections. An engine restarted from CoLocated to Lan in that window is refused by name by the server rule. One restarted from Lan to CoLocated is published chunked: the content is verified and identical, but the route is not the declared one. Accepted and documented.
Hash cross-check timing. A mismatch is detected only after the engine has issued the revision (additive, invariant 30). The Protocol error must say not to take it.

R9 trap. services/editor/src and Editor/shell/src must never contain a Locality:: path in a match arm, a comparison, matches! or if let. The matches! regex scans to the next ';' (check-boundaries.mjs:361). This design keeps Locality entirely out of that source; cfg(test) modules are stripped (check-boundaries.mjs:226-230).

R1/R4. cmd_publish's parameters must stay free of document types. Because no new Tauri command is added, SHELL_READ and generate_handler! stay untouched. Any later 'show the package folder' command must be added to both.

Folder agreement holds by construction only when the host and the Editor share one user's cache_root (platform.rs:96-102). Under different accounts, or a folder with no write permission, the result is a named refusal (WritePackage, PackagePathOutsideDirectory or PackageUnreadable), never a mis-route.

Orphans. A crash between write and removal, or a failed removal (for example a Windows sharing violation after a transport error mid-read), leaves one inert, uniquely named .gpxpkg that is never offered again. 5.10 adds no sweeper; that is a follow-up.
Invariant 22 debt. The hand-mirrored TS PublishResult (main.ts:218-225) gains two fields instead of being generated.

Supersedes the 5.8 evidence line that the Editor 'never builds a package' (docs/evidence/5.8/README.md:18-20). The 5.9 done-when 'the Editor's publish sends every asset ... through preflight and the 5.3 transfer' now holds only over a LAN; co-located, the path handoff replaces it. Record both in docs/evidence/5.10.

'Both are taken' passes only on a T0 engine. Below T0 the take is a named TierTooLow SKIP (conformance/src/asset_route.rs:138-148; invariant 43), so done evidence must come from the T0 workstation, not CI.
The 'LAN' worker is a loopback worker started with --lan, which 5.8 accepted. It is not a second machine.

Out of scope, recorded only: ADR-001 B.1 (Proposed) still draws an Editor control link (docs/adr/0001-distributed-architecture.md:330-337). 11.65 (engine preview through a control-plane Render) and 14.4 (Editor viewport media profile) will hit the same R6/5.7 wall. mocks/mock-editor still publishes asset-less scenes with publish_scene (mocks/mock-editor/src/main.rs:139-152).

Environment: during this read-only pass the C: temp volume had 0 MB free and a grep failed with 'No space left on device'. cargo, conformance scratch directories and packages under cache_root all need space.
test_plan: Precondition: free space on the C: temp volume. It reported 0 MB free during this pass.
Regression: the 5.8 package_handoff_suite and the 5.9 asset_route_suite pass unchanged. 5.8's forced-path check against the LAN worker still gets PackageDirectoryNotConfigured.
Full gate on the T0 workstation: npm run check exits 0 (fmt, clippy -D warnings, Node, Editor, Rust, conformance). The 5.10 Take checks must be PASS there, not SKIP.

alternatives.name: Relayed declaration, zero wire (design 1)
alternatives.summary: Conformance, or a new `gx-engine-host --describe` run by tools/launch-shells.mjs, reads EngineCapability.locality over the control plane and hands it to the Editor as GX_EDITOR_ENGINE JSON {assetPlane, locality, packageDirectory}. The Editor always packages and passes the relayed value to publish_package. Each peer's package_directory is gated by handoff_for(self.locality), and the worker refuses --lan with --package-dir.
alternatives.why_not: The Editor never reads the declaration. It holds a copy taken at launch and keyed to one endpoint, which goes stale across an engine restart or relocation; that is the exact case capability.rs:4-6 warns about. No process can relay a real LAN engine's declaration, because the host reaches only 127.0.0.1 with a tokenless Client (services/render-engine/host/src/lib.rs:144-151), so a LAN publish needs hand-written locality, which is a guess. An Editor started without the launcher (`npm run editor`) refuses every publish. The guard is copied into each peer instead of living as one shared rule. The test only proves that the Editor parses a value the harness relayed. Keep it as the documented fallback if the user rules out any new asset-plane request.

alternatives.name: Design 2 as proposed (asset-plane locality read, directory from the web layer, filesystem work in services/editor)
alternatives.summary: Uses the same {locality:{}} read, required trait method and shared-server LAN rule as the recommendation. In addition, cmd_publish gains a packageDirectory parameter filled from a new UI field and a new cmd_default_package_directory command, and services/editor/src/publish.rs does create_dir_all, write_package and remove_file itself. declaredLocality is sent to the web.
alternatives.why_not: The web layer would hand the shell a free-text filesystem path that the shell then writes into and deletes from, which widens the trust boundary in the shell header (Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:3-9). Filesystem writes in services/editor fall outside STORE_WRITE_ALLOWED in spirit (check-boundaries.mjs:69-72). Sending declaredLocality to the web leaves a standing R9-TS trap. It has the largest surface: a new parameter, a new command, a UI field and an environment variable. Its best parts (the server rule, the worker startup refusal, the LocalityReply Refused arm, the hash cross-check and removal on every outcome) are grafted into the recommendation.

alternatives.name: Carve out R6 and 5.7 for a read-only Editor capability client
alternatives.summary: Allow an Editor-side crate a control-plane client restricted to Capability, with a new role that 5.7's authorise admits for Capability only, so the Editor reads EngineCapability.locality itself.
alternatives.why_not: It weakens the structural enforcement of invariant 4 (a capability the Editor lacks is absent from it, Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:3-9). It requires changing R6 (check-boundaries.mjs:67-68, 370-373), 5.7's Playout-only authorise (Shared/control-plane/src/message.rs:93-95) and invariant 55's 'capability is not public'. It is the only option that keeps the 5.10 wording literally, but it reopens a boundary the user closed deliberately. It is worth a separate decision only if 11.65/14.4 later need a broader Editor read.

alternatives.name: Editor-configured locality (setting next to the endpoint, or inferred from 'a package directory is configured')
alternatives.summary: The operator sets the locality, or the Editor infers co-located when a package directory is set, and the Editor passes that value to publish_package.
alternatives.why_not: This is a second declaration that can disagree silently. --lan and --package-dir are independent and both bind loopback (worker main.rs:50-54, 72-103, 134-139). The by-path handler checks only the directory (publish.rs:386-394). It contradicts 'declared, not probed' (capability.rs:4-6) and makes an L0-to-L1 move an Editor reconfiguration instead of a deployment change (invariant 16).

alternatives.name: Probe and fall back (try by path, chunk on refusal)
alternatives.summary: Offer the package by path first, and switch to the chunked upload on PackageDirectoryNotConfigured or PackageUnreadable.
alternatives.why_not: It is forbidden by 'declared, not probed' and by 'decided here and nowhere else' (capability.rs:4-6; handoff.rs:6-8). The by-path client is crate-private (publish.rs:248-251). A silent fallback breaks the refusal contract (invariants 17-18), and the route would follow the directory configuration instead of the declared locality.

alternatives.name: Infer locality from the address (loopback means co-located)
alternatives.summary: Treat a 127.0.0.1 asset endpoint as CoLocated and anything else as Lan.
alternatives.why_not: It is forbidden by capability.rs:4-6 and wrong in practice: the --lan worker and the mock both bind loopback (worker main.rs:134-139; mocks/mock-engine/src/main.rs:80), so it would disagree with the 5.8/5.10 LAN worker immediately.

alternatives.name: Engine-side offer and decide (option 3b)
alternatives.summary: The publisher offers a package (path plus hashes), and the engine applies handoff_for to its own locality, replying either 'taken by path' or 'send the missing hashes'.
alternatives.why_not: It needs a new negotiation message and a different publish_package signature (today it takes the locality, handoff.rs:213-217). It contradicts 5.8's done-when 'the publisher chooses path or chunked upload from the declared locality' (GrapiX-Build-Plan.md:316) and reopens a done row. The recommendation gets the same 'only the engine's declaration decides' property with the shared-server LAN rule instead.

alternatives.name: Keep publish_with_assets for the LAN route and add publish_package only for co-located
alternatives.summary: The Editor chooses between its existing 5.9 chunked path and the 5.8 by-path publisher from the locality.
alternatives.why_not: Choosing the publisher from the locality in Editor code is an R9 violation (check-boundaries.mjs:245-246, 361-364). It also leaves two publish routes, against invariant 60's one command path. publish_package needs a package on disk for both routes (handoff.rs:213-256), so 'always package' is the R9-clean shape.

decisions_for_user.question: Where does the Editor learn the engine's declared locality, given that R6 bars any Editor-side control-plane client and 5.7 answers the control port only for Role::Playout?
options: (a) A new one-field asset-plane read {locality:{}}, answered from the engine's single locality field. Conformance holds it equal to EngineCapability.locality on the real workers and both mocks.

(b) A zero-wire relay: gx-engine-host --describe or the launcher reads EngineCapability over the control plane and passes it to the Editor as GX_EDITOR_ENGINE. A real LAN engine then needs hand configuration, and the copy goes stale on restart.
(c) Carve out R6 and 5.7 for a read-only Capability client with a new role. This amends the structural enforcement of invariant 4.
(d) An Editor configuration setting for locality. This is a guess that can disagree silently.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: (a). It is the only option where the Editor reads the engine's own declaration fresh on every publish without a control client. Keep (b) documented as the fallback if (a) is refused.

decisions_for_user.question: Is the 5.8 decision 'Nothing new goes on the wire or into EngineCapability' scoped to the package directory, or does it also rule out a new asset-plane locality read?
options: Scoped to the package directory. That is how docs/evidence/5.8/README.md:20-22 reads, as the sentence after 'a co-located publisher is configured with the engine's package directory'. A locality read is allowed.
It covers all new wire. Then only option (b), the relay, remains, and the 5.10 test can prove only that a relayed value is passed through.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Scoped to the directory. The package directory still never goes on the wire, and no field is added to EngineCapability.

decisions_for_user.question: Reword row 5.10's name and done-when? The current text, 'reads the engine's declared locality from the capability exchange', cannot be executed under R6 and 5.7.
options: Adopt the proposed rewording in row_5_10_rewording: the locality comes from the engine itself on its asset plane and is held equal to EngineCapability.locality by conformance; the publish always packages, has named negatives and mutations, and is done only when both publications are Taken on T0.
Keep the wording and amend R6/5.7 instead (decision 1, option c).
A relay wording ('with the locality the engine declared in its capability exchange, relayed by the process that ran it') if the user picks option (b).
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Adopt the proposed rewording. Also amend the doc comments at Shared/control-plane/src/capability.rs:1-6 and Shared/asset-plane/src/handoff.rs:6-8 to say the declaration is made once, in the engine's locality field, and is carried by both planes.

decisions_for_user.question: Can an 'Editor-path test' live in conformance? Conformance may take, and it calls the same gx_editor::publish function cmd_publish calls. The Editor/shell test itself cannot take, because R6 forbids a control client even as a dev-dependency.
options: Conformance calls gx_editor::publish::publish_document, the production function cmd_publish uses after the logic moves into services/editor, and takes there. Editor/shell/tests/publish.rs covers routes and refusals without a take.
Add gx-editor-shell (a Tauri crate) as a conformance dependency so it can call the shell function directly.
Take nowhere and assert only the publication.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: The first option. It keeps Tauri out of the harness and still exercises the Editor's own path, and the row's 'both are taken' stays satisfied by conformance, never through the Editor (invariants 4 and 5).

decisions_for_user.question: Harden the engine so a LAN-declared engine never reads a package path?
options: Both: one rule in the shared asset-plane server (a LAN-declared peer has no effective package directory, refused PackageDirectoryNotConfigured) and gx-render-worker refusing --lan with --package-dir at startup (exit 2).
The server rule only. A worker started with --lan and --package-dir then silently ignores its directory.
Neither. A stale or forged CoLocated offer to a LAN engine that has a directory is accepted silently.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Both. The server rule gives worker/mock parity by construction (invariant 45), and the startup refusal turns a silently ignored flag into a named usage error. No existing caller combines the two flags.

decisions_for_user.question: What happens when the Editor publishes to a co-located engine started without --package-dir? 5.9's chunked publish worked in that case.
options: A named refusal (PackageDirectoryNotConfigured, with the Editor's folder appended). The launcher and gx-engine-host pass --package-dir so the normal dev and host paths work; a hand-started worker needs the flag.
The worker defaults --package-dir to platform::package_exchange_root() when co-located. This widens the engine's default read surface and changes 5.8's default.
The Editor falls back to chunked. This is probing and a silent substitution, forbidden by capability.rs:4-6 and invariant 18.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: A named refusal, with the launcher and host passing the folder. Restart the running dev pair once through the updated launcher.

decisions_for_user.question: Where is the Editor's package folder configured?
options: GX_EDITOR_PACKAGE_DIR if set, else a new platform::package_exchange_root() (cache_root/packages). The launcher passes the same folder to the worker, and gx-engine-host spawns workers with --package-dir package_exchange_root(). There is no UI write path.
A cmd_publish packageDirectory parameter plus a UI field, which lets the web layer choose a path the shell writes into and deletes from.
A persisted per-machine Editor settings file. None exists today, and project.json travels with the project, so it is the wrong home.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: The environment variable plus the platform default. A read-only display of the folder can come later through a SHELL_READ command if wanted.

decisions_for_user.question: Accept these Editor behaviour changes and record them in the 5.10 evidence: assets with no content hash are refused PackageAssetNotPackaged at publish; the shell's publish, publish_with_assets and scene_asset_bytes are retired so there is one route; and the 5.9 row gets a note?
options: Accept all three, and add a note to row 5.9: '(after 5.10: over a LAN; a co-located engine is handed a package by path)'.
Accept the code changes but leave the 5.9 row text untouched and note it only in docs/evidence/5.10.
Keep publish_with_assets as a second entry point. This means two publish routes, against invariant 60.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Accept all three and add the 5.9 note, so the plan does not describe a co-located behaviour the Editor no longer has.

decisions_for_user.question: Done evidence and the 'real LAN worker': is a loopback worker started with --lan acceptable, and must both takes be Taken on the T0 workstation?
options: Yes to both. This is the same as 5.8 (loopback --lan worker) and 5.9 (below T0, TierTooLow is a named SKIP; done only when Taken on T0).
Require a second machine for the LAN half. That needs Phase 14's off-loopback exposure and asset-plane authentication first.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Yes to both. Also record that Phase 14 must authenticate the asset plane, the new locality read included, before any port is exposed beyond loopback (invariant 55).

decisions_for_user.question: Resolve now the wider question of how the Editor reads from the engine (ADR-001 B.1's Editor control line, 11.65 engine preview through a control-plane Render, 14.4 Editor viewport media profile)?
options: Defer. 5.10 adds only the locality read; record the open question in the 5.10 evidence and in ADR-001 as stale text to amend.
Decide now that the asset plane is the Editor's carrier for every engine self-description.
Decide now on an R6/5.7 amendment for a read-only Editor engine client.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Defer. Decide it with 11.65, when a Render request makes the requirement concrete.

row_5_10_rewording: | `5.10` | Editor publishes by the engine's declared route: by path when co-located, chunked over a LAN (added 8 Nov 2026, user decision, split from `5.8`; reworded <date>, user decision: the Editor cannot read the control-plane capability exchange, because R6 bars a control client and 5.7 answers the control port only for Playout, so it reads the same declaration from the engine on its asset plane) | BE | 5.8, 5.9 | The Editor's publish (`cmd_publish` → `gx_editor::publish::publish_document` → `gx_asset_plane::publish_as_package`) learns the engine's declared locality only from the engine itself. It sends a closed `{locality:{}}` read to the asset-plane address it publishes to, and the engine answers from the same field it declares as `EngineCapability.locality`. The Editor holds no control-plane client (R6) and names no `Locality` (R9). The publish always writes one verified package, named by content hash and never by user text, into its package folder: `GX_EDITOR_PACKAGE_DIR` if set, else `platform::package_exchange_root()`. The launcher and `gx-engine-host` give a co-located engine that same folder as `--package-dir`. The package is published through `gx_asset_plane::publish_package`: co-located by path with 0 asset bytes, over a LAN chunked with only the missing bytes. It is removed after the reply. A LAN-declared engine reads no package path, and `gx-render-worker` refuses `--lan --package-dir`. Nothing about the directory goes on the wire or into `EngineCapability`. A conformance suite runs against two real workers (one with `--package-dir D`, one with `--lan`) and both mocks. It shows each peer's asset-plane answer equal to the `EngineCapability.locality` read over the control plane. It publishes the Inter lower third from an Editor `AssetStore` through the functions `cmd_publish` calls, with folder D, to each worker: `LocalPath` with 0 bytes and the package inside D, and `ChunkedUpload` with exactly the font's bytes. Both publications are Published with the document's content hash, D is empty afterwards, and the harness takes each with its pinned hash: Taken on the T0 workstation, a named skip below T0. The suite also shows each of these refused by name as `PublishRefused`, never `Unreachable`: a folder outside D, a co-located worker without `--package-dir`, and a path offered to a LAN-declared engine that holds a directory. An asset with no content hash is refused before any socket opens. Mutations of the declared value, of the peer's answer and of the server rule each fail a check. `npm run check` passes with check:boundaries clean. |
